overall: Conversational and plain, like a reporter walking someone through the record. Start on the first word with no lead-in and keep the connecting words moving. Carry each line's emphasis through stress on its one phrase, never through volume, and never add a triumphant note to a fix or a completed step. Take natural breaths at commas and sentence ends, and run 'flood remedy' straight into 'as currently under development' with no breath. Keep every hedge (may, could, interim, currently) audible inside its own phrase. Land the final phrase quiet, level and complete, with no rising tone at the end. Take one short, audible breath right after "in February" before "in a limited area", and one short, audible breath right after "the flood remedy" before "as currently under development". Each breath is a natural clause edge of about a quarter second, never a long hold and never a drop in energy, and the sentence stays connected through it. After that second breath, start the closing phrase with a clearly voiced word "as", pronounced "az", given its own small stress so it is never swallowed or heard as "is", then continue "currently under development" level and complete.

lines.energy: after a natural breath, level and unhurried, plainer than the opening Then level and a touch lower, carried straight on Then quietest line in the film, steady, falling and complete, with a short audible breath after "the flood remedy" before "as currently under development", and the word "as" after that breath is clearly voiced and pronounced "az", never swallowed.
